newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end up slightly,foreign funds buy.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end up slightly,foreign funds buy.

text.p: Colombian stocks gained slightly as foreign investment funds snapped up shares in banking and manufacturing in an otherwise sluggish session.

The Bogota IBB index ended 0.49 percent higher at 866.99 on a thin volume of 1.3 billion pesos. Trading in Medellin was also depressed. Its IBOMED index ended at 13,514.68 on a volume of 1.2 billion pesos -- a modest 0.46 percent rise.
"You need a lot of optimism to believe that a drop in interest rates could have a major impact on the stock market," one trader said.

He doubted that announcements by the Central Bank that it would be injecting 1.1 trillion pesos ($970.6 million) into the banking system and cutting banks' legal reserve requirement by 5 percent would have much impact on the markets. Such measures have in the past contributed to keeping interest rates down.
"Investors are paying more attention to companies' balance sheets, which are apparently not too good, rather than to possible cuts in the interest rates," the trader added.
The main mover in the Bogota exchange was supermarket chain Carulla, which rose 3.7 percent to 5,600 pesos.

Cement manufacturer Cementos Caribe ended up 2.58 percent at 4,001 pesos on a 40.7 million peso volume. Brewing giant Bavaria finished the day 1.84 percent up at 3,870 on a 202.4 million pesos volume.

"Gains in Cementos Caribe and Bavaria were prompted by small purchases by foreign funds that did not want to buy up large blocks of shares at the risk of sparking a big movement in the market," another Bogota broker said.
The bulk of the session's trading centered on Banco Ganadero ordinary shares, which rose 0.70 percent to 284 pesos and on Banco de Colombia, which remained unchanged at 436.
